newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally on Telmex record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally on Telmex record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks moderated earlier gains, but still closed sharply up on foreign demand for blue chips, traders said.

Traders drew attention to market heavyweight Telmex L shares, which soared 46 centavos to equal a March 19 record close of 16.58 pesos. Telmex ADRs, meanwhile, rose 1-1/8 to 42-1/4, a level unseen since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
Final closing figures placed the leading IPC share index up 29.48 points, or 0.76 percent, at 3,834.58.
Traders added Telmex prices declined at the close from an intraday high of 16.92 pesos, which also explained why the IPC receded from a maximum of 3,871.72 points
"They took profits on Telmex towards the close and that basically is why the bourse ended off session highs," a floor trader said.
Analysts said traders in both Mexico and New York had bought on a favourable outlook for first quarter earnings.
"Market feeling is Telmex will post earnings per ADR of $1.04, up from previous forecasts of $0.90-$0.95," said an analyst, who asked not to be named.
Traders said gains on the bourse were also driven by the Dow Jones, which rose sharply for the second day in a row, surging 92.71 points to 6,679.87.
Lower-then-expected increase in domestic primary rates also encouraged investors to buy Mexican stocks, traders said.

Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 22.61 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a gain of 28 basis points since last week, compared with an increase of 83 basis points forecast in a previously conducted Reuters survey.
"Dealers were positive albeit somewhat selective. They liked the outcome of the primary auction and that was reflected in foreigners who stepped into the market," a trader said.
"Furthermore, several blue chips rebounded that the market had previously hit hard, like GFB and Televisa," he added.

The presence of foreign dealers pushed up trading volume to a very heavy 163.4 million shares traded. Financial group GFB B shares gained 16 centavos to 2.70 pesos, while media group 1.90 pesos to 104.00 pesos.
Holding company Accelsa headed the prominent gainers' list .PG.MX, up 18 centavos to 1.88 pesos.
"There is market talk that Accelsa has signed a major manufacturing agreement and dealers may also be buying on a favorable earnings outlook," a floor trader said.
Accelsa officlas were not available for comment.

Debt-ridden conglomerate Sidek topped the leading decliners' list .PL.MX, down two centavos to 30 centavos, followed by retailer Grupo Salinas y Rocha, down four centavos to 63 centavos following sharp speculative gains on takeover rumours since denied by the company.
